title: Regulatory Reporting Analyst
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also <a href="https://monzo.com/savings">save</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/investments">invest </a>and <a href="https://monzo.com/pensions">combine their pensions</a> with us. </p> <p>With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!</p> <p>We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️</p> <hr> <p> </p></div><p>📍London | 💰up to £55,000 (depending on experience) ➕ incentive awards tied to your performance | <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Benefits</a> | <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U62l09nB0M4">Hear from the team</a> ✨ </p> <p><strong>⭐Our Regulatory team</strong><strong><br></strong></p> <p>We are looking for<strong> </strong>a curious, adaptive and data-focused <strong>Regulatory Reporting Analyst</strong> with a strong attention to detail to join our regulatory reporting team at Monzo. The team is responsible for understanding our prudential regulatory reporting requirements, working on projects and submissions relating to these and collaborating with teams across Monzo.</p> <p><strong>🔑 You’ll play a key role by…</strong><strong><br></strong></p> <ul> <li>Producing Monzo’s regulatory liquidity reporting, ensuring robust and consistent controls across all outputs to support regulatory compliance and internal governance requirements</li> <li>Documenting the applicable regulatory interpretations and communication</li> <li>Assisting the wider team produce Monzo’s capital and liquidity regulatory reporting and disclosures (including Pillar 3)</li> <li>Executing and improving the controls required to ensure regulatory reporting is timely, accurate and complete</li> <li>Ensuring all our regulatory reporting runs like clockwork</li> <li>Using data visualisation tools to build dashboards and facilitate sign-off and useful insights</li> <li>Designing brilliant ways to automate your work and leverage technology to ensure we scale with the business</li> </ul> <p><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong><strong><br></strong></p> <ul> <li>You have a good understanding and experience of producing LCR, NSFR, PRA110, ALMM returns</li> <li>You’re excited by data and have a sharp eye for detail</li> <li>You have knowledge of coding languages like SQL would be a bonus, although a willingness to learn is just fine </li> <li>You have a proven record of delivering to strict deadlines </li> <li>You want to automate or enhance recurring processes, particularly by leveraging technology, but know how to balance this with getting the actual reports out!</li> </ul> <p><strong>🙌 What’s in it for you</strong></p> <p>💰up to £55,000 (depending on experience) ➕ incentive awards tied to your performance</p> <p>📍This role is based in our London office on a hybrid basis. We expect 1 - 2 days per week working from the office.</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. </p> <p>📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.</p> <p>🏡 £200 allowance to spend on your work-from-home setup after completing your first full month with us.</p> <p>➕ Plus lots more! <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Read our full list of benefits</a>.</p> <p><strong>🌈</strong><strong> The application journey has 4 key steps</strong></p> <ul> <li>Phone call with recruiter (30 mins)</li> <li>Initial call with hiring manager (30 mins)</li> <li>Technical interview with hiring manager and team member (45 mins)</li> <li>Monzo behavioural interview (30 min)</li> </ul> <p>This process should take around 3-4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible! <br><br>We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out.</p> <p>#LI-NZ1</p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/diversity-and-inclusion">blog</a>, 2026 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/our-2026-diversity-and-inclusion-report" target="_blank">Diversity and Inclusion Report</a> and 2025 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/gender-pay-gap-report-2025">Gender Pay Gap Report.</a></p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.</p> <p>If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊</p></div>

title: Senior VFX Artist & Animation Generalist
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>Who We Are: </strong></p> <p>Gram Games is the studio behind popular titles like 1010!, Six!, Merge Dragons!, and Merge Magic!, with more exciting projects in the pipeline. We are proudly part of the Zynga & Take-Two Interactive family. We do things differently here: we work in small self-managing teams, giving you an incredible amount of ownership, autonomy, and impact. </p> <p>At Gram, everyone is expected to have a razor-sharp focus on creating a tangible impact on their team, their work environment, and on the overall company strategy. If you are motivated by autonomy, constant improvement, collaboration, and a sense of belonging, this is the place for you.</p></div><p>The New Games team is looking for a highly skilled Senior VFX & Animation Generalist to join us. This is a hands-on and creative role for someone who can take visual effects and motion design from ideation to final in-game implementation. You will help design, build, and polish the VFX and motion language of the game, working closely with art, design, tech art, engineering, and production.</p> <p>Crucially, we need someone who can take full ownership of the pipeline that drives the dynamic, deeply satisfying VFX and interactions seen in top-tier, highly polished casual puzzle games. We are looking for a generalist who combines strong artistic judgment with deep hands-on Unity experience.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities </strong></p> <ul> <li>Own, build, and optimize the VFX and animation pipeline, establishing efficient workflows tailored to producing the highly dynamic and rewarding interactions expected in top-tier casual puzzle games.</li> <li>Create high-quality VFX and animations from ideation, concept, and visual exploration through to final implementation in Unity.</li> <li>Design and implement "juicy" interactions and celebratory effects that make every player interaction feel incredibly tactile and satisfying.</li> <li>Bring your own creative ideas to the table to make the puzzle pieces, UI, environments, and effects feel alive and responsive.</li> <li>Work hands-on with modern Unity workflows, including the Animation timeline, Particle System, Shader Graph, URP, custom materials, and animation-driven effects.</li> <li>Translate concepts, prototypes, gameplay needs, and rough ideas into clear, polished in-engine effects and motion.</li> <li>Optimize VFX and animations for mobile, balancing visual ambition with performance, memory, readability, and production constraints.</li> <li>Identify visual, technical, and workflow bottlenecks in the pipeline, and propose practical solutions.</li> <li>Collaborate with tech art and engineering on shaders, tools, profiling, and runtime performance.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Significant experience (at a Senior, Lead, or Principal level) creating real-time VFX and animations for games, specifically casual puzzle games or highly polished free-to-play titles.</li> <li>Proven experience owning, building, or significantly contributing to a VFX and animation pipeline for mobile.</li> <li>A strong grasp of fundamental animation principles applied to gameplay elements, UI, and effects.</li> <li>Strong hands-on experience making VFX and animations directly in Unity.</li> <li>A strong portfolio showing high-quality in-game VFX and motion design from idea to final implementation, highlighting "juicy" and satisfying visual feedback.</li> <li>The ability to create assets from early ideation, concept, mood boards, mockups, prototypes, or rough direction and turn them into polished in-engine results.</li> <li>A strong understanding of mobile performance constraints and optimization techniques.</li> <li>The ability to troubleshoot visual bugs, sorting issues, and performance problems.</li> <li>Strong collaboration skills across art, design, technical art, engineering, and production.</li> <li>A proactive, organized, and self-driven approach to your work.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What Makes You Successful In This Role</strong></p> <ul> <li>You are not waiting for tasks to be assigned. You look at the game, understand what it needs, and help raise the bar.</li> <li>You are comfortable owning a feature’s VFX and motion from start to finish: shaping the idea, exploring the visual direction, implementing it in Unity, polishing it, and keeping stakeholders informed and aligned.</li> <li>You can explain your creative and technical choices clearly, take feedback well, and help the team make better visual decisions.</li> <li>Most importantly, you make the game feel better and the player feel profoundly rewarded.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What We Offer You: </strong></h4> <ul> <li>Highly competitive salary</li> <li>Private medical care</li> <li>Company bonus scheme</li> <li>Awesome onsite chef serving breakfast, lunch, and lots of treats (naughty and nice)</li> <li>Life insurance and a favorable pension scheme</li> <li>Healthcare cash plan including dental and optical coverage</li> <li>Amazing tech to work with and consoles to play and relax with everywhere you look!</li> </ul> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p>We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, which means we are committed to creating and celebrating diverse thoughts, cultures, and backgrounds throughout our organization.  Employment with us is based on substantive ability, objective qualifications, and work ethic – not an individual’s race, creed, color, religion, sex or gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin or ancestry, alienage or citizenship status, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, status as a victim of domestic violence or sex offenses, reproductive health decision, or any other characteristics protected by applicable law.</p> <p>As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to providing the necessary support and accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities, health conditions, or impairments (subject to any local qualifying requirements) to ensure their full participation in the job application or interview process. Please contact us at <a ---------- to request any accommodations or for support related to your application for an open position.</p> <p>Please be aware that Zynga does not conduct job interviews or make job offers over third-party messaging apps such as Telegram, WhatsApp, or others.  Zynga also does not engage in any financial exchanges during the recruitment or onboarding process, and will never ask a candidate for their personal or financial information over an app or other unofficial chat channel.  Any attempt to do so may be the result of a scamp or phishing attack, and you should not engage.  Zynga’s  in-house recruitment team will only contact individuals through their official Company email addresses (i.e., via a zynga.com, take2games.com, naturalmotion.com, smallgiantgames.com, themavens.com, gram.gs email domain).   </p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Software Engineer, Developer Experience
description: About Docker Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout. We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default. _______________________________________________________________________ The Developer Experience team builds the backend systems and product capabilities that help developers understand, secure and ship software with confidence. The team powers important parts of Docker Scout, Docker Hardened Images and the workflows that turn supply-chain data into useful developer experiences. Our systems are deliberately polyglot. Today that includes Clojure and Go services, event-driven workflows, Kafka, legacy Datomic components and newer Spanner-backed services. We will keep evolving the stack as the product and business change. We are looking for an adaptable backend engineer who can become effective in an unfamiliar codebase, choose technology pragmatically and help other engineers do the same. Clojure experience is useful, but it is not a requirement and this is not a Clojure-specialist role. We make extensive use of AI-assisted engineering tools. We expect engineers to use them thoughtfully, validate their output and remain accountable for the quality, security and operability of what ships. At Staff level, you will also help the team turn good individual practice into repeatable workflows, controls and shared standards. As a Staff Software Engineer, you will lead ambiguous, cross-team work from problem definition through measurable outcomes. You will remain hands-on in code while shaping architecture, raising operational standards and creating enough clarity for several engineers and partner teams to move quickly. Work may span developer-facing features, build and artefact workflows, data and event pipelines, platform evolution and integrations with Docker's build and security systems. Success in This Role Looks Like You will succeed by finding the highest-leverage problem, creating momentum before every detail is known and bringing people with you. Within your first year, teams should be delivering more confidently because you have made system boundaries clearer, reduced operational risk, connected technical choices to customer outcomes and helped senior engineers take on larger work. Responsibilities Set technical direction for major backend and developer-experience initiatives across Clojure, Go and adjacent systems. Turn ambiguous product or platform problems into clear plans, staged decisions and measurable outcomes. Design, build and operate distributed services, event pipelines, databases and APIs with strong security and reliability characteristics. Lead cross-team delivery, surface risks early and remove technical or organisational blockers without waiting for formal authority. Make pragmatic recommendations about when to retain, evolve or replace existing components, including the continued reduction of legacy Datomic dependencies. Partner with Product, Design, Security and other engineering teams to connect technical investment to developer and business outcomes. Improve observability, incident readiness, performance and service ownership across the Developer Experience estate. Improve engineering leverage through appropriate automation, AI-assisted workflows and controls that preserve human accountability. Mentor senior engineers, raise the quality of design and code reviews and create reusable patterns that multiply the team. Stay hands-on through implementation, debugging and the team's paid on-call rotation. Communicate decisions and trade-offs clearly in a remote, async-first environment. Qualifications Required 8+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated technical leadership on production systems at scale. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience Deep experience designing, building and operating production backend or platform systems. Strong programming ability in at least one production language, with evidence of becoming effective in unfamiliar languages and codebases. Experience with distributed systems, event-driven architectures, APIs, relational or distributed databases and cloud-native infrastructure. A track record of leading complex initiatives that crossed team or organisational boundaries. Strong technical and product judgement, including the ability to explain constraints, alternatives, customer outcomes and business trade-offs. Evidence of influencing without authority and improving the effectiveness of other experienced engineers. An operational mindset that treats observability, resilience, incident response and on-call ownership as part of engineering. Comfort using AI-assisted engineering tools critically while retaining ownership of the result. Clear written and spoken communication suited to a remote, async-first company. Helpful, but not required Production experience with Go, Clojure or both. Experience with Spanner, Datomic, Kafka or other distributed data and streaming platforms. Experience with build systems, containers, artefact workflows or developer tooling. Experience evolving a platform, database or language strategy without disrupting product delivery. Experience building security or software supply-chain products. What to Expect First 30 Days Build context on Developer Experience products, customers, architecture and current priorities. Pair across Clojure, Go, Datomic and Spanner-backed systems and ship a useful production change. Understand the operational profile of the team's services, including on-call and recurring failure modes. Build working relationships with Product, Design, Security and adjacent engineering teams. Learn the team's AI-assisted engineering practices and identify where shared controls or workflows would improve them. First 90 Days Lead the technical framing and delivery plan for one significant team or cross-team problem. Contribute production code in the parts of the stack needed to move that work forward. Identify and begin addressing a material reliability, observability, data or architectural weakness. Establish a mentoring and design-review cadence that helps other engineers own larger decisions. One Year Outlook (First Year) Be a trusted technical leader for Developer Experience and a sought-after partner across Docker. Deliver at least one material product or platform outcome spanning multiple teams or systems. Improve the reliability, clarity and delivery speed of the backend and data estate. Shape pragmatic evolution across Clojure, Go, Datomic, Spanner and future technologies without turning technology choice into the goal. Grow other senior engineers into broader ownership and reduce the number of decisions that depend on a small set of people. Docker considers sponsorship on a case-by-case basis based on business needs. Compensation & Equity EU: €110,500 – €181,500+ equity United States: $170,350 – $275,550 + equity ______________________________________________________________________ Posting Information Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role. AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process. Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent. ______________________________________________________________________ Perks & Benefits Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration. Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work. Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break. Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success. Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work. Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning. Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment. Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow. Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country. Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old. Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community. #LI-REMOTE Compensation: €110.5K – €181.5K • Offers Equity • Multiple Ranges EU Salary Range • EU Salary Range €110,500 – €181,500 • Offers Equity US Salary Range • US Salary Range $170,350 – $275,550 • Offers Equity Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Software Engineer, Secure Build
description: About Docker Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout. We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default. _______________________________________________________________________ The Secure Build team builds and operates the infrastructure behind Docker's container builds. The team owns Docker Build Cloud and Auto Builds while developing the next generation of trusted build and CI capabilities. Software is being changed faster than ever, but CI remains a bottleneck and a major trust boundary. Developers and software agents need to run build and test work quickly without exposing secrets, losing local-to-cloud parity or accepting an unverifiable result. Our direction is to make Docker the trusted place CI runs and turn that constraint into an accelerator. The technical work spans Go services, container and build technology, cloud infrastructure, isolated execution and software supply-chain security. It also requires disciplined operation of the production systems customers rely on today. Docker Build Cloud and Auto Builds will need targeted reliability and operational improvements while useful capabilities evolve towards a coherent Secure Build platform. As a Senior Software Engineer, you will turn these problems into practical product and technical outcomes. You will own substantial work from discovery and design through production, make sound security and reliability trade-offs, and stay close to the experience of developers and the agents they delegate work to. We make extensive use of AI-assisted engineering tools. We expect engineers to use them thoughtfully, validate their output and remain accountable for the quality and security of what ships. Success in This Role Looks Like You will succeed by becoming an end-to-end owner for secure, reliable build infrastructure. Within your first year, you should have delivered a material secure-build or CI capability, reduced operational risk in Docker Build Cloud or Auto Builds, and become a trusted partner to the teams and customers that consume the platform. Responsibilities Turn developer, agent and security problems into clear requirements, staged technical decisions and measurable outcomes. Design, build and operate Go services and APIs that power Docker's build and secure-CI infrastructure. Develop isolation, identity, policy, provenance, attestation and signing capabilities for trusted build and test jobs. Work with container, OCI, BuildKit, cloud and isolated-execution technologies to deliver secure and reproducible workflows. Own features from technical design through rollout, observability, incident response and ongoing maintenance. Keep Docker Build Cloud and Auto Builds reliable, make targeted improvements that reduce operational load, and help their capabilities evolve towards the wider Secure Build direction. Make practical security trade-offs and use threat modelling to guide designs without blocking delivery. Design for a clear developer experience, including workflows initiated or consumed by software agents. Partner with Product, Security, Developer Experience, Registry and other platform teams on end-to-end customer workflows. Participate in the team's paid on-call rotation and drive improvements from incidents and recurring operational work. Communicate decisions, risks and progress clearly in a remote, async-first environment. Qualifications Required 6+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated technical leadership on production systems at scale. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience Strong backend engineering experience building and operating distributed systems in production. Production experience with Go and the ability to write, test, review and debug maintainable Go services. Experience with containers and build or CI systems, such as OCI, BuildKit, Buildx, GitHub Actions or comparable platforms. Experience with cloud-native infrastructure and a major cloud platform. A strong operational mindset covering observability, reliability, incident response and on-call ownership. Evidence of taking a feature or service from an ambiguous problem through production operation and measurable results. Working knowledge of security boundaries, identity, secrets and common software supply-chain risks. A strong product mindset and care for developer workflows, including experiences used by software agents. Clear written and spoken communication suited to a remote, async-first company. Helpful, but not required Experience with Kubernetes. Experience with SLSA, in-toto, SBOM, VEX, Sigstore, cosign, provenance or artefact signing. Experience with sandboxing, microVMs, untrusted workload execution or multi-tenant infrastructure. Experience building hosted CI runners, remote builders or developer-platform infrastructure. Experience with agentic development workflows or building systems used programmatically by software agents. Experience evolving a legacy production system while delivering new capabilities. What to Expect First 30 Days Build context on Docker Build Cloud, Auto Builds and the Secure Build product and technical direction. Pair with the Secure Build team on core services, deployments and operational practices. Ship a useful production change and take part in an operational review or incident-learning session. Understand the secure-CI threat model and build relationships with DHI, Registry and Developer Experience. First 90 Days Own a secure-build feature or reliability improvement from problem definition through production. Contribute materially to the secure-CI architecture, including isolation, identity, policy or signed evidence. Deliver an observable improvement to the reliability or operability of an existing build service. Demonstrate strong product judgement across developer and agent workflows. One Year Outlook (First Year) Be a trusted senior technical owner on the Secure Build team. Deliver a material secure-CI or trusted-build capability used by customers or internal product teams. Improve the reliability and maintainability of Docker Build Cloud and Auto Builds while helping their useful capabilities converge with the wider platform. We are looking for a freelance Lead Enterprise Architect to run a fixed scope enterprise architecture review for a large UK professional services firm, and to stay on as the firm’s interim architect if the client takes the follow on work. You will lead the work day to day. Intelance’s engagement partner stays accountable for the engagement and the client relationship. The review runs over four to six weeks from November 2026 and needs around 18 days. The optional follow on is two days a week for eight weeks, then a short check around 90 days after the review, finishing around early March 2027. The work is mainly remote within the UK, with some days at client offices in England agreed in advance. Tasks Lead the review from the first meeting to the final presentation, as the client’s day to day contact. Start from the records the client already keeps, such as integration documents, system lists and project records. Run eight to ten one hour conversations with the heads of applications, IT operations, data, client solutions and the project office. Build one clear picture of the whole technology estate: systems, connections, data flows and owners. Trace two or three recent technology decisions from the first request to the current owner. Write a priority risk report and three costed options for how the firm should own technology decisions, always including keeping its current model. Present the findings and options to the Chief Operating Officer with Intelance’s engagement partner. If the follow on goes ahead, act as the firm’s interim architect two days a week. Set up a technology decision forum, prepare the first three decisions for it and hand over the estate map as a working tool. Requirements Experience as a lead or head of enterprise architecture in a UK law firm, or in another professional services partnership of around 1,000 people or more. You have set up an architecture function, design authority or technology decision forum from scratch. Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics 365 and the Power Platform. Knowledge of Aderant, InterAction or legal document management systems is a strong plus. You write costed options papers yourself and present them with confidence to a Chief Operating Officer or board. You work well alongside capable internal teams and build on what they already have. Independent of software vendors. You must not currently work for, or resell products from, a legal software supplier, a Microsoft partner or an IT services provider to the client. Available from early November 2026 to early March 2027, at three to four days a week during the review. Based in the UK with the right to work here, and willing to complete the background checks the client requires. Benefits £750 to £850 per day, depending on relevant experience. Rates exclude VAT where applicable. Contracting route and tax status are confirmed before work starts. Around 18 days for the review, plus around 16 days and a day 90 check if the follow on goes ahead. A defined scope, clear outputs and Intelance templates, so your time goes on the work itself. Direct work with Intelance’s engagement partner, with a Data and AI Architect alongside you. The possibility of an ongoing part time architect role with the same client, by mutual agreement. No minimum volume of work is guaranteed. Apply with your CV and answer the short screening questions. No cover letter is needed. Shortlisted candidates will join a working session with our engagement partner to talk through how they would run the review. The work starts once the client confirms the engagement. We will agree availability, rate and contract terms in writing before then. Please do not include confidential client documents. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Associate - Venture & Growth
description: <p>Senior Associate - Venture & Growth (m/f/d)</p> <p><strong>Join the team rewriting the rules in private markets.</strong></p> <p>Moonfare delivers what few others can: the highly sought-after funds and hidden-gem investments that go beyond what most private banks offer. Every opportunity is subjected to a ruthless vetting process; the bar is unforgivingly high. The result? Institutional-quality portfolios for investors who demand more.</p> <p>Our team combines finance veterans with talent from tech, consulting, law and industries you’d never expect. Headquartered in Berlin, we operate from eight offices across Europe, the US and Asia.</p> <p>If you're ready to build what's next in private markets, let's talk.</p> <p><strong>Mission:</strong></p> <p>Turn Moonfare's access to the world's leading venture managers into a steady, well-underwritten flow of single-company investments our clients can actually buy.</p> <p><strong>About the role:</strong></p> <p>A significant share of Moonfare's AuM sits in venture and growth, and the direct side of it, co-investments and secondaries in VC-backed companies, is where the business is growing fastest. Right now that dealflow arrives faster than we can review it, which puts the deployment of our proprietary funds at risk and caps how far the direct platform can scale. The scope of this role begins the moment an opportunity reaches us and ends when the deal closes, so operations sits outside it, as does the client raise itself. Your first year is weighted towards screening, pipeline and diligence, with the sourcing and business development side building from there as your market view and relationships deepen. You will work alongside senior members of the team rather than alone, and what moves forward is decided together.</p> <p><strong>The team:</strong></p> <p>Venture & Growth sits inside Moonfare's Investment team and runs two connected things. One is a multi-manager vehicle making primary fund investments into leading VC and growth managers across the US and Europe, where we have historically backed Founders Fund, a16z, Accel, Lightspeed, Khosla and General Catalyst. The other is the direct programme of co-investments and secondaries that those manager relationships generate, which is where this role's centre of gravity sits. You will report to the Head of VC & Direct Investing and work daily with the commercial team, who depend on you for qualified dealflow, and alongside Legal and Operations to close deals and launch the SPVs we distribute on the platform.</p> <p><strong>You will:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Own the direct deal pipeline. </strong>Everything from the moment an opportunity reaches us through to close is yours to run, so nothing sits unscreened and no access window quietly closes while we are still deciding.</li> <li><strong>Screen inbound co-investments and secondaries, and bring a view to the team. </strong>You run the first pass on what reaches us and form a position on it. What progresses is decided together with the Head of VC & Direct Investing and the wider team, so the value of your screen lies in the quality of the argument you bring to that conversation and in how sharply you separate the two or three worth our time from the rest.</li> <li><strong>Run diligence on direct deals. </strong>The core of it is judgement on the business itself: how good the company is, how strong the founding team is, how large and how contested the market is, and whether the thesis survives contact with the evidence. The technical layer sits underneath, with cap table analysis, preference stacks and waterfalls, and pricing and NAV work on secondary positions, so we know exactly what we are buying and at what price. You will do this with support from senior members of the team, and contribute to primary fund diligence alongside the direct mandate.</li> <li><strong>Author the investment memos that go to IC. </strong>The committee decides on what you put in front of it, so a memo with a gap in it, an inaccuracy, or a risk nobody spotted becomes a decision made on the wrong basis.</li> <li><strong>Build the market view, and then the market position. </strong>Relationships with intermediaries, GPs and, over time, founders are what get us into constrained opportunities and keep us current on where secondaries are pricing. This part of the role grows as you do, and watching how competitors structure and go to market belongs to it, because that is what keeps us competitive on price.</li> <li><strong>Help make the process repeatable. </strong>You will refine how we diligence direct deals and contribute to the sourcing, screening and monitoring tooling behind it, including AI-enabled approaches, so the volume we can handle is not capped by how much a person can read.</li> <li><strong>Turn deals into something our clients can buy. </strong>The commercial team depends on this seat for qualified dealflow and for support packaging opportunities into investor-ready materials. Fund deployment runs at the pace this work sets.</li> </ul> <p><strong>The next Moonfarian:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Four or more years centred on venture and growth investing. </strong>That comes along one of two paths. Either direct investment expertise, sourcing and diligencing investments in technology companies at a venture capital, growth equity or crossover fund, or an allocator seat focused on VC and growth where you have underwritten co-investments hands-on. Directly relevant adjacent backgrounds include TMT and technology investment banking, tech-focused private equity or software buyout, corporate development or corporate VC at a technology company, and consulting with a tech or commercial diligence focus. What matters most is a demonstrable track record of hands-on deal work: screening opportunities, running diligence, and taking a view through to a decision.</li> <li><strong>A network in venture you can already use. </strong>This one is non-negotiable. Relationships with GPs, intermediaries such as placement agents and bankers, and other LPs and co-investors, enough to get us access to constrained opportunities, support diligence and track spin-out candidates. You do not need the network of someone twice your experience. You do need a real one, and you will build a much larger one here.</li> <li><strong>Investment judgement you can defend. </strong>You form a view on a company and argue it, including the case against. You can read a business and a founding team, size a market and test a thesis against what the evidence actually supports. You are genuinely fluent in emerging technology and can develop conviction on themes and business models, with AI front of mind but not the only lens. You assess attractiveness quickly on limited or imperfect information, you are comfortable with financial modelling and market analysis, and you know your way around cap tables, preference stacks and waterfalls, secondary pricing, VC term sheets and SPV mechanics. You can hold several live opportunities at once and prioritise sharply between them.</li> <li><strong>An entrepreneurial instinct, which matters here as much as the investing. </strong>This one is non-negotiable too. This is a builder's seat as much as an investor's. You want a hand in structuring, go-to-market, process design and the operational scaffolding of a business line that is still being built. Your AI fluency goes past using the tools to designing processes around them.</li> <li><strong>Communication that works in three different rooms, and relationships that outlast any one deal. </strong>You can pitch and tailor to an investment committee, to a commercial team, and to clients, and prepare the reports and presentations each of them needs. Just as important is what you build over time with GPs and intermediaries, the standing that makes them think of us when something scarce comes up, because that is what turns a contact list into access. Excellent written and spoken English is essential.</li> </ul> <p><strong>How the role is measured: </strong></p> <ul> <li>Deals sourced, screened, and taken through to IC.</li> <li>Timely deployment of Moonfare's proprietary funds, such as the Moonfare Technology Fund.</li> <li>Allocation secured with GPs and intermediaries, meaning access we would not otherwise have had.</li> <li>Whether IC can decide on your memos without rework, and whether risks surface in diligence rather than after close.</li> <li>Capital raised on direct deals and the performance ultimately generated. These are programme outcomes you contribute to rather than own alone, and they are read that way.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What success looks like:</strong></p> <p><strong>By six months, </strong>the deal pipeline runs without the Head of VC & Direct Investing having to chase it. Opportunities are screened as they arrive, you are bringing a formed view on each one to the team, and the queue is visible to everyone who needs it.|<br><strong>By twelve months, </strong>deal review is fully operationalised, with a process the team can run rather than one person's habits, and more than ten direct deals have been through IC.</p> <p><strong>This role is unlikely to be a good match if you</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Prefer to let relationships develop slowly and mostly in writing.</strong> Much of our access comes from conversations with managers and intermediaries you do not know yet, and someone reserved about starting them will find the sourcing half of this job hard going.</li> <li><strong>Want a defined process to work inside. </strong>A good part of what this role runs does not exist yet, and you would be designing it while live deals are moving.</li> <li><strong>Want sole authority over what you invest in.</strong> We discuss deals as a team and decide together what progresses, which means your view gets argued with before it gets acted on. If you want to run your own book without that, this will frustrate you.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What your growth could look like:</strong></p> <p>The next step from here is Associate Principal. Getting there means leading the majority of diligence processes rather than running them with support, and having a network that generates opportunities rather than one that keeps you informed.</p> <p>What you get here that you would not get at a fund: you join the Head of VC & Direct Investing in GP conversations from early on and inherit access to a built-up base of manager relationships. You see the commercial side of raising capital for a deal alongside the investment side, which most investors never touch. And you help build a wider business, across a discretionary fund, capital raising for individual deals and, in time, a secondary market.</p> <p><strong>If you feel you do not meet all of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply!<br></strong></p> <p><strong>We can only accept applications from those eligible to live and work in Berlin/London. This is a hybrid role with office attendance required 4 days/week.</strong></p&gt

title: Senior Backend Engineer - Ledger Platform
description: Senior Back-End Engineer - Ledger Platform Hybrid in London (UK) or Remote within the UK We’re looking for a Senior Back-End Engineer This role is a chance to tackle complex, high-impact challenges at the heart of our fintech platform. You will join the team that owns iwoca's ledger — the system of record for the money we lend and collect — and you will be responsible for scaling it across the full lifecycle of our credit card and lending products, building the reconciliation and reporting that prove it correct, and laying the foundations for our next generation of products. This is a hands-on role: you'll design these systems, write the code, and own them in production. The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team The Ledger Platform team owns the ledger across all of iwoca's products, from credit cards to our lending range, plus everything around it: reconciliation, financial reporting, and the data Finance, Accounting and Capital Markets run on. We work closely with a Product Manager, shipping frequently and owning our systems in production. Some of the team work fully remotely and others are hybrid, working 1-3 days per week in the London office. The role Responsibility and Autonomy: Lead the delivery of projects involving many stakeholders and systems. Go beyond the code to develop deep expertise in our domain — our core financial products and our stakeholders' needs — and become a trusted technical advisor to the business. Perform detailed technical scoping and prototyping to support feasibility testing and decision making. Delivery and Collaboration Architect and implement scalable solutions for complex challenges: the lifecycle of an account, interest and repayment allocation, reconciliation, and how financial data reaches our reporting stack. Use domain modelling to find the simple design behind a complicated problem, and structure software so that it is easy to understand, test and evolve. Be pragmatic about which parts of a problem actually need solving now. The hardest work here is deciding what not to build. Build solutions that avoid single points of failure, and make sure our releases happen with zero downtime. Translate ambiguous product requirements into clear, actionable technical plans that guide the team's work. Promptly investigate and fix live issues, and ensure they do not resurface. Own what you ship in production and keep it reliable and easy to operate. Contribute high-quality, production-ready code and foster a collaborative environment by reviewing work and writing useful documentation. Learning and Growth: Work with the team to improve our development and agile practices and raise our engineering standards. Share new approaches and tooling with the wider engineering group through our internal forums and company-wide talks. AI: We're pushing hard on AI-assisted development. Engineers here write clear technical specs, let skills and agents implement boiler-plate, and hold a high bar on code review — the person, not the model, is accountable for what merges. We expect AI output to be validated for correctness, performance and security like any other change. We give the team unlimited tokens across all models and expect people to experiment. The requirements Essential: Extensive back-end engineering experience. Experience building and running microservices and distributed systems in production. Comfortable reasoning about durable cross-service communication, transactional correctness, and failure modes at scale. Extensive experience with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, but open to MySQL or similar (e.g., MS SQL, Oracle); emphasis is on data integrity. Experience with systems where correctness is a hard requirement — ledgers, accounting, billing or payments, ideally in a regulated setting — including the invariants, immutable audit trails and reconciliation controls that enforce it. Experience leading a feature or project end to end — scoping, design, delivery, and running it in production. You use AI (like Cursor, Claude Code or similar) in your daily flow - whether for work or for fun. You use it to blast through boilerplate and research, so you can focus on the hard parts: complex architecture, rigour, and high-stakes decision-making. A strong technical or mathematical foundation, evidenced by a degree in a quantitative field (Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Maths or similar) or equivalent professional experience. You work well as a peer: pairing on hard problems, giving useful code review, and unblocking teammates day-to-day. Clear written and verbal communication — you can explain a technical trade-off to Finance, and a business constraint back to engineers. Bonus: A background in high-logic or high-scale fields like Fintech, Gaming, Healthcare Tech, Logistics, Security/Cryptography or similar. Working knowledge of modern data tooling - ideally Snowflake and dbt - used to build analytical or reporting pipelines. Knowledge of messaging frameworks and event-driven patterns (e.g. Kafka). The salary We expect to pay from £80,000 to £110,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews. The culture At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time. The offices We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work: Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks. Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions. The benefits Flexible working hours. Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership. A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses. A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents. 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave. A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years. Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support. 3% Pension contributions on total earnings. An employee equity incentive scheme. Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money. Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme. Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield. And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer: A learning and development budget for everyone. Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers. Access to learning platforms like Treehouse. description: Backend Engineer - Repeats Hybrid in London, United Kingdom (At least one day in office per week) We're looking for a backend engineer to join the Repeats team. You will work on the services that decide which repeat customers get a loan, at what price, and how much they can borrow. These sit at the heart of iwoca's back book. The company Imagine a world where every small business has the power to thrive. That's the world we're building at iwoca. Small businesses aren't just statistics – they're the heartbeat of our communities, the character of our high streets, and the engine of our economy. Since 2012, we've revolutionised how these businesses access finance, turning what was once a lengthy, frustrating process into something remarkable: funding that's fast, flexible, and actually works for modern businesses. Our impact speaks for itself: we've provided billions in funding to over 150,000 businesses across Europe, making us one of the continent's leading fintech innovators. But we're just getting started. Our mission? To empower one million businesses with the financial tools they deserve. We combine cutting-edge technology and data science with genuine human understanding to make finance feel less like a barrier and more like a superpower. Whether it's managing cash flow or seizing unexpected opportunities, we ensure businesses get the funds they need – often within minutes. The team The Repeats team is one of iwoca's funnel teams. We grow customer lifetime value after a business's first loan. That means we own the underwriting, pricing, and product experience for two segments that make up most of iwoca's back-book value: top-up customers who borrow again while still repaying, and loan-ended customers who return for a new loan. Almost every repeat borrower goes through code we own. The team is cross-functional – backend, frontend, product, design, data science and analytics – shipping behind split tests and measuring impact in Looker rather than on gut feel. The role Your first project will be the re-architecture of our flex-loan repeat offer pipeline: the flow that decides who is eligible for a new loan, what they pay, and how much they can borrow. This area has been under-invested for years. Once the new pipeline is in place, product has a clear runway of features ready to ship on top of it. You will own backend features end-to-end, from design through to shipping and monitoring them in production. Over time, you will pick up front-end work and grow into a full-stack role. Impact on customers Work on the systems that shape every repeat customer's offer, and move the metrics behind iwoca's back-book performance. Ship features that make it faster and clearer for small business owners to access follow-on funding. Ownership and delivery Work through the full development lifecycle – from technical design and implementation to rollout behind a split test – on well-defined components. Maintain and support the core services behind repeat lending: the lending_decision app inside iwoca-django, the repeats pricing and offer-amount services, and the customer account pages. You care how your work affects customers, and use experiments and metrics to guide decisions. You have experience of writing automated tests and take code quality and safe releases seriously. You use it to blast through boilerplate and research so you can focus on the hard parts: complex architecture, rigour and high-stakes decisions. title: Senior Backend Engineer - Customer Operations Platform
description: Senior Software Engineer - Customer Operations Platform Hybrid in London, UK (1-2 days per week) We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer iwoca’s operational tools and processes are a competitive advantage, allowing us to give great customer service, manage risk, and get money into our customers’ hands as quickly as possible. You’ll join our growing Customer Operations Platform team to help improve the systems that power these processes, building tailored flows for our Operations teams, automating processes using AI, using ML models to make smarter decisions, and improving the reliability of our communication services. You’ll work closely with our Operations teams, getting user feedback and input on requirements from users working in the same building, and seeing the impact of your changes on the people you work with. The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The role As a Senior Engineer you’ll run projects end to end, work out what' s actually needed, design it, build it and look after it in production. Responsibility and Autonomy: Take the lead on complex projects that span many systems and many stakeholders — e.g. CRM, telephony, contact, and task management Build a strong understanding of the business context: how our ops teams actually work, how the processes you're automating are supposed to run, and what the people relying on your systems need from them. Do the detailed technical scoping and prototyping that tells us whether an idea is feasible before it reaches the roadmap. Write fluent technical documents and developer tickets distilling product requirements into clear and actionable technical work. Build relationships with key stakeholders including Operations Strategy, Credit Analysts, Account Managers, and Collections teams. Learning and Growth: Mentor junior developers, fostering a learning environment that encourages experimentation and innovation. Embody our growth mindset mentality by sharing new technologies and best practices within the team as well as more broadly across the company. The projects Here are some of the most recent problems we are solving: iwocaChat. Operations staff spend a large share of their day assembling context from multiple systems before they can help a customer. iwocaChat uses Claude to answer those questions directly, so staff spend their time on the customer rather than the lookup. Migrating the monolith. We are incrementally moving business logic out of our Django monolith into smaller, independently deployable services. Because it cuts across every domain, you'd be shaping service boundaries and ownership models that stick around long after the monolith is gone. Inbox messaging reworking. We are replacing our third party email inbox application with an inhouse solution, utilising AI to enable operations staff to automate the actions of our most frequent customer service enquiries. The requirements Essential: Experience developing and owning shared back end services that other engineering teams contribute to and depend on - being the trusted reviewer for their contributions and shaping how they build on top of your work. Experience building and shaping distributed systems in complex business domains. Ability to translate complex operational needs into technical architecture. Strong capability using AI tools to automate routine tasks and research, enabling greater focus on complex system architecture and critical technical decision-making. You use AI (Cursor, Claude Code or similar) in your daily flow – whether for work or for fun. You use it to blast through boilerplate and research so you can focus on the hard parts: complex architecture, rigour and high-stakes decisions. Bonus: Commercial experience with Python frameworks like Django. Familiarity with front-end technologies (React, TypeScript) and browser debugging. Experience with complex data architectures, including event-sourced data models. The salary We expect to pay from £80,000 - £110,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews. The culture At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective. We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. title: Enterprise Account Manager - UKI
description: About Us Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem . Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work. At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team. Visit www.perk.com to learn more. About the role: As our Account Management team grows we are looking for a customer-oriented and result-driven Enterprise AM to join us. As an Enterprise Account Manager you will be actively contributing to our continued customer satisfaction as well as working to increase growth and margin within existing accounts. In this role you will be responsible for a portfolio of top accounts. You must possess a genuine hunger to navigate your accounts in a fast-changing, hyper-growth environment, be ready to roll-up your sleeves and work hard. What You’ll Do Own a portfolio of Tier 1 customers, building trusted relationships with champions, key decision makers, and executive stakeholders across Finance, Procurement, Travel, HR, IT, and Leadership. Build and execute strategic account plans by developing a deep understanding of your customers' business, identifying expansion opportunities, mitigating risks, and maximising long-term customer value. Identify growth opportunities across business units, geographies, and product lines to expand your portfolio through new business opportunities, upselling, and cross-selling. Drive adoption across Perk's Travel and Spend platform by identifying underutilised features, expanding use cases, and partnering with customers on change management initiatives. Leverage data and analytics to lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), delivering reports and presentations that demonstrate business outcomes, product adoption, ROI, and future strategic opportunities to senior stakeholders. Be an expert across Perk's Travel and Spend platform to educate customers on new capabilities and consistently meet or exceed quarterly expansion targets. Identify common challenges within each account, develop timely solutions, and implement long-term strategies that improve customer outcomes and satisfaction. Be Perk's biggest advocate within your customers and your customers' biggest advocate within Perk by partnering with Product, Engineering, and Technical Support teams to resolve issues, influence product improvements, and represent the voice of the customer. Effectively prioritise your time and resources to maximise impact across your portfolio and key business initiatives. What We're Looking For Significant experience managing a portfolio of Tier 1 customers in a SaaS, travel-tech, fintech, or spend management environment. Experience working with finance, procurement, travel, or expense management ecosystems is a strong plus. Proven ability to build relationships across Finance, Procurement, Travel, HR, IT, and executive leadership within large enterprise organisations. Experience navigating complex enterprise organisations with multiple stakeholders, procurement processes, and executive decision-makers. Outstanding presentation and communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels and build trusted, long-term relationships. Strong financial, commercial, and analytical acumen, with the ability to discuss T&E policy, spend controls, ROI, cost optimisation, and operational efficiency with finance leaders. Results-oriented mindset with a strong focus on customer satisfaction and long-term customer value. Excellent prioritisation and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities across a portfolio of strategic accounts. You can focus on accomplishing big wins and never get lost in less important ideas that are floating around Growth Mindset: You seek feedback early and often and are open to both give and take constructive and direct criticism Experience using inside sales tools like Salesforce, Google Tools, Zendesk, Looker. title: Team Lead, Account Development Representatives
description: Are you ready to unlock intelligence? If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others. About the Role: Kong is hiring an ADR Team Lead to support our NEMEA region: the UK, Benelux, and Nordics. This is a player-coach role. You'll carry your own pipeline targets while taking an active hand in developing the team around you, especially the newer ADRs still finding their footing. You'll work closely with, and report into, the Senior Manager for NEMEA. You're shaping how the team operates, not running it solo. Think of this as a high-impact individual contributor role with a leadership layer built in: the natural next step for an ADR who's ready to start making other people better, not just themselves. Our NEMEA team is already strong. Driven, independent, hitting their numbers. What they need isn't more oversight. They need someone who sharpens how the team works, especially around process and tooling, while making sure newer reps get the support to ramp fast. You'll report to Oscar Winberg. He moves fast, sets a high bar, and expects people to bring solutions, not just flag problems. He's direct, so you'll always know exactly where you stand, and he expects that same directness back: if you disagree, he wants the pushback, backed by data, not silence. Earn his trust and he'll hand you real ownership. What he won't do is hand-hold, so this role suits someone who'd rather be given room to run than told exactly what to do. What You'll Do: Carry your own number. You'll hit your own pipeline targets as an active ADR. Your activity and results set the standard for everyone watching. You'll contribute to weekly forecasting alongside the Senior Manager. Support newer ADRs. You'll be the first point of contact for less tenured reps, helping them ramp faster and build good habits early. You'll help with onboarding alongside the Senior Manager and Enablement, and run regular 1:1s with newer ADRs. Different reps need different things from you, so you'll read where each person is and adjust your coaching accordingly rather than running the same playbook on everyone. You'll help build individual development plans grounded in a real read of each rep's attitude, process, and results, and you'll flag underperformance early, with context, instead of letting it fester. Coach and upskill the team. You'll support team coaching sessions: live dialling, pitch practice, feedback loops. You'll run or contribute to upskilling initiatives, on your own or with Enablement. You'll share what's working, best practices, sequences, outbound approaches, with the wider team, and give direct, specific feedback often, recognizing strong work and not letting bad habits slide. Sharpen process and tooling. You'll help spot where the team's workflows and tooling could run more efficiently, and support the Senior Manager in rolling out improvements without stripping reps of their autonomy. You'll be the go-to person for best practice on Salesforce, Outreach, and the team's automation tools. Contribute to the wider GTM motion. You'll keep strong alignment with your AE partners and take part in pipe review cadences. You'll support the Senior Manager in preparing performance updates and regional insights, and join bi-weekly RD cadences where it makes sense. What You'll Bring: Hands-on ADR or SDR experience. You know what this job feels like from the inside, not just what it looks like from a deck. A real coach's instinct. You get energy from making other people better, not just from hitting your own number. The ability to juggle competing priorities without dropping the ball. Your own quota, coaching newer reps, and process work will all pull on your time in the same week, and you know how to decide what actually matters right now. Strong time management. This is one we screen for directly, not something we assume comes with experience. A bias for building. You spot what needs fixing and go build it, rather than working only through a list of tasks someone else handed you. Analytical rigor. You make calls based on data, not gut feel, and you're comfortable being specific about why a number moved, including when that number is going the wrong way. You touch the line. Your metrics back it up: leading indicators (activity, sequence execution, pipeline hygiene) and lagging indicators (quota attainment, pipeline generated) that show a track record of real discipline, not one good quarter. Real trust with your AE and RD partners, earned through consistency, not just alignment on paper. Transparency, especially with leadership, especially when something isn't on track. We'd rather hear it early than find out later. The kind of presence the team actually looks up to, not just reports to. Comfort in an allbound model with a heavy outbound emphasis. Self-awareness and a genuine investment in growing as a leader. Language skills relevant to the UK, Benelux, or Nordics are a bonus, not a requirement. We'll consider strong internal and external candidates. For external hires, the bar is high: we're looking for someone who brings something genuinely differentiated. Culture and Values: The EMEA SDR team are weather makers. We don't wait for opportunity, we create it. We're accountable, relentless, and we invest in each other like no other team does. Relentless. Energy and intention every day. Every challenge is a chance to get stronger. Character. Good humans first. Integrity, humility, and keeping our word. Together. No one gets left behind. Differences make us better, not harder to manage. Truth. Radical honesty. We say the hard things with care. That's how we move fast. Accountable. We own our results, bias toward action, and don't wait to be told. Pioneering. We take up space, experiment, and bring creative thinking to every challenge. In NEMEA specifically, we operate in mature markets. We don't manufacture urgency, we earn entry by knowing the landscape better than the prospect does. We're pipeline gardeners: patient, precise, persistent. "We don't book meetings. We build pipeline." This role is a genuine development opportunity. For the right person, it's the foundation of a leadership career at Kong. Interested? Reach out to Oscar Winberg to discuss. #LI-TR1 About Kong: Kong Inc., the AI Connectivity Company, is building the connectivity layer of AI. Trusted by the Fortune 500® and AI-native startups alike, Kong’s unified API and AI platform enables organizations to secure, manage, accelerate, govern, and monetize the flow of intelligence across APIs and AI traffic — on any model, any cloud. For more information, visit www.konghq.com . Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Quality Assurance Associate AVP
description: Quality Assurance Associate Glasgow About the Role We are seeking a Quality Assurance Associate to support the delivery of high-quality customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence reviews. This role is responsible for conducting independent quality assessments of completed client files, ensuring they meet regulatory expectations, internal policies, and operational standards before final approval. The successful candidate will play a key role in strengthening quality controls, identifying areas for improvement, and supporting the delivery of a robust financial crime compliance framework. Key Responsibilities Conduct quality reviews of completed due diligence files, including higher-risk customers, politically exposed persons (PEPs), complex ownership structures, and individuals or entities subject to adverse media or sanctions considerations. Assess the quality and completeness of customer risk assessments, source of wealth/source of funds evidence, beneficial ownership verification, and overall case rationale. Review screening outcomes and ensure decisions, escalations, and risk-related findings are appropriately documented and supported. Capture and report quality review outcomes, categorising findings according to materiality and risk impact. Provide constructive feedback and coaching to case analysts, supporting improvements in accuracy and consistency. Monitor recurring themes and error trends, contributing to process enhancements, guidance updates, and training initiatives. Produce quality assurance reporting and management information, highlighting key metrics, trends, and areas of focus. Maintain awareness of evolving AML and financial crime regulatory requirements and ensure these are reflected within quality review standards. Assist with internal reviews, audits, regulatory enquiries, and assurance activities where required. Skills & Experience Previous experience within KYC, CDD, EDD, Financial Crime Operations, or a related compliance environment. Strong understanding of AML regulations, risk-based due diligence principles, and enhanced due diligence requirements. Experience reviewing complex client structures, source of wealth/source of funds information, and adverse media findings. Excellent attention to detail with the ability to evaluate information critically and make balanced risk-based assessments. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide clear and actionable feedback. Comfortable working with client lifecycle management and screening platforms. Experience within a quality control, quality assurance, oversight, or review function would be advantageous. Relevant AML, KYC, or financial crime qualifications are beneficial but not essential. How We Work: Delta Capita is an equal opportunity employer. We positively encourage applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of age, colour, disability, national origin, ancestry, race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. If you require any reasonable adjustments through your interview process, please use the designated space within the application questionnaire. This is a contract role-based Glasgow. As the selection and interview process is ongoing, please submit your application in English as soon as possible, if your profile is selected, a member of our team will contact you within 4 weeks. For this role, a valid working permit for Singapore is mandatory. Who We Are: Delta Capita Group (a member of the Prytek Group) is a global managed services, consulting, and solutions provider with a unique combination of experience in Financial Services and technology innovation capability. Our mission is to reinvent the financial services value chain providing technology based mutualized services for financial institutions for non-differentiating services.
